newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - India hits Tuesday blues after rally.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - India hits Tuesday blues after rally.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) gave up all of Monday's gains as the local market failed to follow up the GDR market gains and Grasim reported weak earnings.
"There had been quite a lot of marking up issues on Monday and they simply got marked down again on Tuesday in not very active trade," said a broker.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index closed down 3.02 points, 4.56 percent, at 63.14 points, with the premium over the local market at 17.28 percent compared with yesterday's 18.77 percent.
The Capel Index had risen 4.64 percent on Monday, but sentiment turned negative when it became clear the Bombay market was not going to share in the rally when it opened on Tuesday.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index closed down 32.26 points at 3,139.33.
Among losers GDRs in Grasim, which reported a 13 percent fall in first half earnings to 1.47 billion rupees, fell 30 cents to $13.50/$14.50.
Hindalco GDRs, which had risen 45 cents yesterday, fell back 50 cents to $18.25/$19.25 on Tuesday.
"It went up and then back down as buyers failed to get excited. The market will probably stabilise in a narrow range for the rest of the week," said a trader.
The Capel Korea GDR Index fell 1.03 points, 1.50 percent, at 67.70, a premium of 29.77 percent after the Korea Composite Index ended 3.77 points lower to a provisional 747.05.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index closed up 3.03 points, 3.37 percent, at 93.20, a premium of 1.84 percent after the Taiwan Weighted Index rose 28.16 points or 0.42 percent to 6,687.88.
